newsitem.title: USA: Plot leader nursed hatred for Israel, U.S..
newsitem.headline: Plot leader nursed hatred for Israel, U.S..

text.p: Ramzi Ahmed Yousef, convicted on Thursday of masterminding a plot to bomb 12 passenger jets, has said U.S. support of Israel gives Palestinians and Lebanese the right to attack targets in this country.

The 28-year-old defendant, who represented himself at his trial with the help of a legal adviser, faces another trial this year on charges he orchestrated the fatal 1993 World Trade Centre explosion. He was one of the world's most wanted fugitives until he was arrested last year in Pakistan and returned to New York.

In the current case, prosecutors alleged that Yousef developed the scheme, recruited the two other defendants Abdul Hakim Murad and Wali Khan Amin Shah, and taught them how to make bombs. All three were convicted in Manhattan on Thursday and could be sentenced to life in prison.

Authorities said the plot to bomb the planes was foiled by a fire last year at an apartment shared by Yousef and Murad in Manila. Philippines police found explosives, bomb making manuals and a laptop computer containing flight information and detonation times.

Yousef fled to Pakistan and was arrested in Islamabad in February 1995. A Secret Service agent testified during the trial that Yousef boasted during his extradition flight to New York that he would have blown up several jumbo jets within a few weeks if his plan had not been discovered.

In March 1995, he released two anti-Israel statements through his court-appointed legal adviser in which he talked of friends and relatives killed by the Israeli army. He said it was of "utmost importance" for the world to know that Moslems will never agree to give up Jerusalem.

"The systematic murder, torture, imprisonment and deportation is ongoing," Yousef said. "The ability of Israel to commit these crimes is the direct result of the considerable military and financial aid which the United States of America provides annually to Israel. And it is this aid which gives Palestinians and Lebanese the right to attack U.S. targets."

Yousef, who has used about a dozen aliases, also said his real name was Abdul-Basit Balochi, that he is from Pakistan, and that he was a trained electronics engineer and explosives expert. He gave his birthdate as April 27, 1968.
The name Abdul-Basit was on the passport and the airplane ticket Yousef used to leave New York the day of the World Trade Centre blast.
